decisions.reason: Changing the battery connector family, pitch, and pinout does not alter the existing overcharge, overdischarge, or thermal-protection requirements.
The selected three-pin connector continues to carry NTC, so the existing requirement to monitor battery temperature through an NTC on J_BAT remains valid unchanged.
The connector specification changes, but the source does not change the established rear placement, orientation, connector-gap, mounting-hole-clearance, or enclosure-fit requirements.
The source decision concerns the battery connector and does not change the USB-C connector or its sourceability constraints.
The battery connector pinout does not change how battery-charge status is displayed through the main-board SK6812 chain.
The battery-interface connector selection does not alter boost-converter enable control or the switched 5V sensor supply.
The source changes the battery connector specification without modifying the TVS-based ESD-protection requirement.
The battery connector change is unrelated to I2C cable length, clock speed, pull-up resistance, or pull-up location.
Selecting a JST-PH connector commonly supplied with batteries does not change the existing general component-availability and fallback-sourceability constraints.
